source: Diocese of Alabama Cycle of Prayer 2025-2026 (Year A)
notes: The source's own cycle runs a full liturgical year, Advent 2025 (30 November 2025) through Christ the King 2026 (22 November 2026) -- per this corpus's one-file-per-diocese-per-year rule, only the 2026 portion (4 January - 22 November, 46 weeks) is transcribed here. The five 2025 dates (30 Nov, 7/14/21/28 Dec 2025) belong in a future episcopal-alabama-2025.json file, not added this pass.

Every single week's entry in the source opens with the identical standing line 'We pray for our Companion Diocese of Honduras and their bishop, Lloyd.' (one week, 1 March, additionally and separately names 'the Diocese of Jerusalem'). Rather than omitting this as decorative boilerplate, it is recorded as the first category subject of every entry -- it is a real, substantive weekly intention, just a repeated one.

This source is a two-column PDF; several weeks' entries continue past a page break, splitting into the top of the next page before the next dated heading. Reconstructed carefully by reading each page in visual column order and checking that no entry's content was dropped at a page boundary (specifically verified for 12 April and 2 August, both of which continue onto the following page).

One line (25 January) reads as a single unbroken phrase in the extracted text -- 'Episcopal Relief and Development Episcopal Ministries' -- with no punctuation separating what may be two distinct items ('Episcopal Relief and Development' the well-known agency, and a separate 'Episcopal Ministries' line) that could have been merged by the two-column PDF extraction. Not confident enough to split it without guessing, so it is preserved as printed, as one category subject.

27 June is printed as '5TH SUNDAY AFTER PENTECOST' continuing the source's own weekly Sunday sequence, but 27 June 2026 is actually a Saturday (checked against the calendar) -- every other date in this file was independently verified to fall on a Sunday. This is very likely a misprint for 28 June in the source's own document; preserved exactly as printed rather than silently corrected, matching this corpus's standing rule.

Per this schema's own definition that a 'parish' subject is specifically a congregation (a parish, mission, or cathedral), several 'Name, City'-shaped lines that are clinics, retirement/senior communities, camps, or other ministries rather than worshipping congregations (e.g. 'Good Samaritan Health Clinic, Cullman'; 'Episcopal Place, Birmingham'; 'St. Martin's in the Pines, Birmingham') are recorded as `category` subjects with the full name preserved, not as `parish` subjects, even though their printed shape matches the diocese's own 'Name, City' parish format. This is an editorial classification judgment, disclosed here as such; the underlying text is unchanged either way.

A small number of longer, list-like intentions that read as one continuous sentence in the source (e.g. 8 March's ministries-to-the-hungry line, 16 August's Diocesan Campus Ministries line) are kept as a single category subject rather than split into several, since the source does not present them as a clean list of independent names.
